WPSS/532/2025

WPSS/531/2025
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J
1. Dr. Kartikey Hari Gupta, learned
counsel for the petitioners.
2. Mr. S.S. Chaudhary and Mr. Narayan
Dutt, learned Standing Counsel for the
State of Uttarakhand.
3. Since the issue involved in both the
petitions is identical, therefore, these are
being heard and decided together by this
common judgment. However, for brevity,
facts of WPSS No. 532 of 2025 alone are
being considered and discussed here.
4. Petitioner belongs to Kahar
community, which is declared as Other
Backward Class (OBC) in State of Uttar
Pradesh as well as in State of
Uttarakhand. Petitioner was born and
brought up in State of Uttar Pradesh and
her parents are permanent resident of
State of Uttar Pradesh, however, upon
marriage, petitioner acquired OBC
certificate from State of Uttarakhand.
5. Petitioner participated in a selection
for appointment as Assistant Teacher,
Government Primary School and she
claimed benefit of reservation available
to Other Backward Classes. Since she
was not selected and recommended for
appointment, therefore, petitioner has
filed this writ petition, seeking the
following reliefs:-
(i) Issue a writ, order in the nature of Certiorari

2026:UHC:2341
quashing the Order dated 28.10.2024 issued by
the Secretary of Government of Uttarakhand,
respondent no. 1 (Contained as Annexure No. 7
to this Writ Petition) and to further quash the
consequential order dated 28.10.2024 issued by
Respondent No. 2 (contained as Annexure No. 8
to this writ petition).
(ii) Issue writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing respondents to issue
Appointment Order in favour of the petitioner
on the post of Assistant Teacher Primary in
District Pauri Garhwal.
6. Learned State Counsel submits that
this Court in WPSS No. 462 of 2025
(decided on 12.11.2025) has held that
marriage will not improve the status of a
candidate and the benefit of reservation
would be available only in the State of
origin and not in the State to which a
candidate migrates on account of
marriage. He, therefore, submits that
relief No. 1 cannot be granted to the
petitioner.
7. This Court finds substance in the
submission made by learned State
Counsel. Consequently, prayer no. 1,
sought in the writ petition, is rejected.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner
then submits that as per the information
received by petitioner, last candidate
selected in General category scored
75.62 marks, while petitioner's score was
a little less at 75.50 marks. He submits
that several candidates belonging to
General category, who were offered
appointment, have not turned up for
joining, therefore, petitioner has a right
to be considered against unreserved
post.
9. Learned State Counsel submits that
if that is so, then petitioner can make
representation to the Competent

2026:UHC:2341
Authority, which shall be dealt with as
per law.
10. Accordingly, the writ petitions are
disposed of by permitting the petitioners
to make representation(s) to the
Competent Authority. If they make
representation(s) within one week from
today, decision thereupon shall be taken,
as per law, within four months thereafter.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J)
